html:
The Goodall focus was a Hopewellian culture of western Michigan and northern Indiana, from about 200 BCE to 500 CE. It is named for the Goodall site in northwest Indiana. "Focus" is an old archaeologists' term for a group of closely similar sites.

Its area ran from the southern tip of Lake Michigan east across northern Indiana to the Ohio border, then north through central Michigan, almost to Saginaw Bay in the east and Grand Traverse Bay in the north. Goodall people built burial mounds and made pottery in the style of the Hopewell peoples further south. They took part in the long trade routes that carried copper, shell and fine stone across the Midwest.

Their neighbours to the east included the Couture and Saugeen peoples. Centuries later the same land was home to the Potawatomi and Miami.
